The number of confirmed exoplanets has grown steadily over time, and older sources now reflect outdated counts. As of 2024, Wikipedia (citing the NASA Exoplanet Archive) lists a total of 5,811 confirmed exoplanets [d3]. NASA's own exoplanet overview page (2023) reports more than 5,800 confirmed exoplanets [d2], consistent with this figure. An April 2024 Reddit post citing NASA data reported 5,602 exoplanets in 4,166 planetary systems [d9], while earlier sources from 2022 and before reported the milestone of "more than 5,000" confirmed exoplanets [d7][d8][d1] — figures that have since been superseded. Beyond confirmed detections, there are also thousands of additional "candidate" exoplanets still awaiting confirmation [d1], and NASA estimates the Milky Way alone contains at least 100 billion planets in total [d4].
